content:
alex: Heads up — saw a cluster of OOMs on prod-gpu-pool-3 last night during long multi-turn sessions. pprof shows KV pages not getting reclaimed, fragments piling up.
maria: :eyes: any spike correlation with kernel selection or batching?
sam: infra-bot alerted at 02:27 UTC with 5 OOM events in 10m window, stack traces point to kv_page_walk stalled on reclaim() + heavy prefix reuse.
infra-bot: [ALERT] gpu-pool-3: 5 x oom_kv_cache within 10m. Pods restarted: 3.
alex: Profiling notes: when we switch to quant-fast-vec kernel (recent canary) memory alignment changed; observed ~8% higher resident memory per KV slab and worse slab fragmentation for long contexts (>8k tokens).
maria: that's interesting — quant kernel is faster per-token but increases fragmentation? can you paste the flamegraph?
alex: pasted blob (trimmed):
```
KV::reclaim() -> page_walk() -> slab_coalesce() ~48%
memalign_overshoot -> pad_gap -> new_fragment_count ++
Batching path: continuous-batching keeps sessions pinned in hot-shard for longer -> reuse window increases -> less frequent evict opportunities
```
sam: So two compounding factors: kernel change increases per-slab overhead, and batching heuristics increase lifetime of prefixes. net = leaked fragments + slow async reclaim -> OOM.
jamie: Do we have repro in staging? any quick mitigations to avoid prod restarts?
alex: Repro in staging with long chat session replay. Quick mitigations I tested locally: 1) throttle continuous-batching max window to 128 tokens for affected model family 2) disable prefix KV caching for sessions > 2k tokens 3) enable aggressive async coalesce (patch diff below).
maria: Can you paste the patch?
alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3210
Patch summary: add heartbeat-driven async_reclaim that triggers coalesce when kv_fragment_count > 1000 OR fragment_utilization < 0.25. Also adds a backoff so we don't run coalesce during peak decode CPU.
sam: Any user-visible regressions from the patch?
alex: Locally: +2ms tail latency p95 on short prompt traffic, but stops the OOM cascade. We can gate by pool label and canary on dedicated pools first.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: rolling canary scheduled for gpu-pool-3-dedicated at 03:30 UTC, batch size 2 nodes.
maria: Longer term we should: 1) add kv metrics (fragment_count, avg_fragment_size, reclaim_latency) 2) add kernel memory-overhead test in CI 3) adjust batching heuristics to bound long-session pinning 4) implement a graceful degrade (fallback model variant with compact KV layout)
alex: +1 on metrics. I added a grafana dashboard draft: /dashboards/kv-page-health (w/ fragment histogram).
jamie: Action list from this thread:
- hotfix (PR 3210) -> canary deploy to dedicated pools (sam)
- throttle continuous-batching for long-context models (maria)
- disable prefix caching for sessions > 2k tokens behind gateway (ops)
- add kv fragmentation metrics & alert (alex)
- run kernel memory-overhead CI test and revert-canary plan (sam)
I've opened INC-2026 and linked PR/graphs.
sam: I'll start the canary. Noting rollback plan: if reclaim_latency > 5s or error_rate increases, revert.
maria: For graceful degradation: propose a server-side fallback that swaps to model_variant=compact-kv (smaller KV slab layout) when free_kv_slots < threshold and session_token_count > 1024. That preserves service but with slightly lower throughput.
alex: Agree. Also add a throttling guard to the router: if kv_frag_count trending up for a pool, route new long sessions to hosted-tier or smaller pools.
jamie: Great. Please add short RFC for the fallback flow (owner: maria) and tag infra for SRE runbook update.
infra-bot: [EVENT] INC-2026 created by jamie. Linked artifacts: PR3210, dashboard draft, staging repro logs.
ops-bot: :thumbsup: marking followups in the oncall checklist.
alex: TL;DR: cause = kernel alignment + longer pinning from batching -> fragment growth -> reclaim stalls -> OOM. Immediate mitigation = canary patch (async coalesce + throttle long batching) + route long sessions away. Plan = metrics + CI + compact fallback.
jamie: Thanks everyone — we'll sync in the 9am eng-runtime stand to decide rollout timing and owners.
maria: copy. will prepare the fallback RFC.
